messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Cost guardrails + model priority (post-demo)

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo time earlier. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can size a pilot and draft pricing: 

1) Monthly token volume range: can you confirm the expected monthly tokens for month 1 vs steady state? On the call you mentioned a ~1M–4M range for initial months and 8M–12M steady state — please confirm if that sounds right. If you can attach the usage export that would be ideal.

2) Target unit economics: you flagged a target of ~$850 / 1M tokens as the internal threshold. Is that an absolute ceiling or a preferred target? If there's a tiered procurement target (e.g., $1,000/1M at low volume, $750/1M at scale), note that too.

3) Model mix by workload: based on your roadmap I want to confirm the expected split so we can recommend routing and quantization profiles. My understanding from Miguel was: chat generation ~65–75%, embeddings for search ~20–30%, and a small rerank/endpoint ~5%. Please confirm the percent ranges and any peak vs baseline differences.

4) Success criteria and pilot length: recommend a 30–60 day pilot with a capped spend. Would you prefer a cost cap or token cap for the pilot?

I attached a very small template (usage-estimates.csv) you can fill out; I also attached our pricing cheat sheet for reference. Once I have the numbers I’ll loop in Karthik to propose a brief pricing sheet (bands + recommended model routings) and Vanessa to pencil in timelines for provisioning Dedicated or Hosted lanes.

Next step: can you send the filled usage CSV by end of week? If helpful I can also take a quick look live on a call.

—Jordan

Subject: Re: Cost guardrails + model priority (post-demo)

Thanks Jordan — quick answers inline.

1) Monthly tokens: initial pilot month estimate ~1.2M tokens (mostly chat previews + search evals). Month 2–3 ramp to ~3.5M, steady state in 6–9 months we expect 9–10M. There will be traffic spikes from seasonal campaigns (~20% uplift) but baseline guidance above is what procurement needs.

2) Unit economics: $850 / 1M is our preferred target at scale. Procurement will accept up to $1,050/1M during the pilot phase if we can show clear quality improvements. We do have a requirement to see predictable per-route pricing (no surprise overage billing).

3) Model mix: current product plan suggests chat generation 70% (customer assistant + checkout flows), embeddings 25% (semantic search + content similarity), rerank 5% (relevance tuning). Peak windows shift more toward chat.

4) Pilot cap: prefer a dollar cap for pilot ($1,250 USD) with a one-week grace window for small overages tied to campaign spikes.

I attached a small export of our telemetry with rough monthly projections. Let us know if you need different granularity.

—Sara
Sara Lin | Head of AI Product, RetailAI
sara@retailai.com

Sara — perfect, thanks for the data and the clarity. Next step from our side: Karthik and I sketched 2 pricing bands for procurement and a model-routing recommendation. High-level: 

- Pilot band (<= 3.5M tokens/month): $1,000 / 1M tokens flat. Includes 30-day pilot support (on-call engineering) and one quality review. Cap you requested: we can hard cap billing at $1,250 for the pilot; any overage would need explicit sign-off.
- Scale band (> 3.5M tokens/month): $820 / 1M tokens with committed 6-month cadence (monthly billing). Tiered discounts available at >10M tokens/month.

Model mix recommendation (initial routing): chat (70%) -> route to rdx-chat-v3 (balanced quantization profile, medium-latency SLO), embeddings (25%) -> rdx-embed-lite (8-bit quantized for cost), rerank (5%) -> rdx-rank (small CPU-friendly endpoint). We recommend sticky routing with fallback to a cheaper chat-lite model during spikes.

We attached a short pricing sketch (redwood-pricing-cheatsheet.pdf) and marked the lines that fit RetailAI’s targets. Karthik — can you confirm the $/1M numbers on Dedicated vs Hosted (latency/SLA delta) and any change to the scale band if they commit to Dedicated? Vanessa — can you check capacity/time to provision Dedicated for a mid-July start? Marissa — FYI on the ask for procurement language and a 30-day pilot T&C.

If that all looks good to RetailAI, we’ll draft a one-page pilot SOW + quickwire DocuSign for procurement.

—Jordan

Looping in details on economics and provisioning: 

- Confirmed: Hosted vs Dedicated delta on listed bands — Hosted pilot ($1,000 / 1M) assumes multi-tenant with 95th percentile latency SLO; Dedicated committed contract can improve to ~$780 / 1M at scale (>10M) due to reserved utilization. The scale band we proposed ($820 / 1M) is feasible for Hosted with a 6-month commit; Dedicated could drop that to $720 / 1M with an annual commit and a standard SLA.

- Cost drivers: chat dominance (70%) means KV-cache memory and higher tail latencies. Embeddings at 25% are very helpful for caching and batching (good unit econ). Rerank 5% minimal.

- Provisioning: Vanessa — Dedicated pool for a starter pilot (1–2 GPUs) can be provisioned in 5 business days once contract is signed and payment method verified; Hosted pilot can be turned on immediately (no infra lead time).

Jordan — I updated the pricing sketch with the dedicated-hosted deltas and added notes on suggested batch sizes and quantization profile names. See attached.

—Karthik
